problem: Field robots for environmental monitoring navigate by pre-specified waypoints and have no model of what visual content the scientist finds relevant, so they cannot search for or attend to particular object types. Labelled underwater data is scarce, and ImageNet embeddings transfer poorly to underwater similarity tasks.
motivation: Scientists (biologists, oceanographers) want to specify data collection at a high level with an exemplar image rather than waypoints. Underwater video has temporal continuity: tracked keypoints give multi-view patches of the same scene part, which can serve as weak supervision with only about 2 hours of human effort instead of a full day of annotation.
key_idea: Learn a visual similarity operator from unlabeled underwater videos (ORB-tracked patch sequences, agglomerative clustering with light human merging, triplet loss) and use exemplar-conditioned similarity heatmaps to steer a robot's camera and navigation.
insight: Weakly supervised cluster merging by a human yields the best patch classification: on Scott Reef 25 F1 is 0.97 vs 0.91 for unsupervised clustering and 0.65-0.81 for ImageNet ResNet18, and on Bellairs Reef F1 is 0.77 vs 0.68-0.71 for ImageNet. Segmentation results are mixed: the ImageNet baseline gets higher Mean IoU on Bellairs (0.40 vs 0.36), so the gains are mainly in classification and retrieval. One exemplar performs about as well as ten, so the representation is stable and cheap to deploy.
method: Patch tracking: ORB keypoints are matched across consecutive frames (top 20 matches under a distance threshold) and 128x128 patches around them are saved as tracked patch sequences; random patches are added for texture-less sand and water areas.

Weakly supervised hierarchical clustering: agglomerative clustering over ImageNet ResNet18 conv5 embeddings of a random patch from each sequence, deliberately over-clustered, then a human quickly merges clusters into k classes.

Triplet training: a shared-weight ResNet18 (ImageNet init, L2 norm, flattened conv5) is fine-tuned with a cosine-similarity triplet loss (margin 0.5), semi-hard mining and Adam (lr 0.0006); anchor and positive come from the same cluster, the negative from another.

Exemplar heatmaps: the exemplar patch descriptor (4x4x512) is slid over the 512x512 image descriptor (16x16x512); the dot-product similarity is upsampled to a heatmap, and heatmaps from several exemplars are merged with optional priority weights.

Informed rolling during diver tracking: the front-camera heatmap (about 10 Hz) is split into 3 regions and the highest-scoring one sets a roll direction in [-90, 90] deg for 10 s so the downward videography camera points at it, while the diver-tracking controller keeps running.

Autonomous search: when the heatmap is highly relevant, the robot detaches from the diver and searches, avoiding obstacles with a BNN imitation-learning visual policy. It then circles the location of interest to alert the diver.

setting.training_data: Unlabeled underwater videos: Bellairs Reef (38 train videos) and Scott Reef 25 (7061 train images), with about 2 hours of manual cluster merging; each dataset trained separately
setting.observation: monocular RGB from front camera (512x512) for heatmaps, plus downward-looking videography camera
setting.action_space: rolling direction in [-90,90] deg; pitch/yaw direction commands for obstacle avoidance; diver-following
setting.simulator: real world only (underwater datasets and field trials)
setting.privileged: none (user-provided exemplar image(s) and human cluster merging at training time)

numbers_note: No standard embodied navigation benchmark is used. Results are patch classification (Scott Reef 25 and Bellairs Reef: Acc/P/R/F1) and segmentation on custom underwater datasets, plus a qualitative field trial (25/40 coral images with informed rolling vs 15/40 with random rolling).
results: Weakly supervised hierarchical clustering reaches 0.97 accuracy/F1 on Scott Reef 25 and 0.78 accuracy (F1 0.77) on Bellairs Reef with 1 exemplar, beating ImageNet ResNet18 (0.68/0.65 and 0.67/0.68 with 1 exemplar; best 0.82/0.81 and 0.73/0.71 with more exemplars), CVAE and IIC. In a field trial on the Aqua robot, informed rolling recorded 25/40 coral images vs 15/40 for random rolling.
limitations: Field evaluation is anecdotal, with one representative comparison (25/40 vs 15/40) and no statistical analysis or navigation metrics.

Semantic segmentation gains over ImageNet are inconsistent (ImageNet is better on Bellairs Mean Acc and IoU), and the IIC comparison is not like-for-like (uninitialized ResNet50 vs pretrained ResNet18).
Requires human cluster merging and separate training per dataset; the navigation policy is a simple 3-region rolling heuristic, not planning.
builds_on: Gupta et al. video representation learning
Manderson et al. underwater visual navigation (BNN imitation policy)
